levels.name: No reliable performance surface
levels.description: The target scenario cannot be resolved or has no discoverable performance surface (no UI to profile, no buildable surfaces, no resolvable Code Facts).
entry_criteria: A scenario id or path is provided
exit_criteria: The scenario resolves and at least one performance axis (build, startup, or UI browser perf) is applicable

levels.name: Capture tier decided
levels.description: Performance Health can decide the reachable browser-perf capture tier for the scenario from Code Facts (no UI -> skipped; non-React UI -> Tier 0; React UI -> Tier 1 reachable) without assuming React from the filesystem.
exit_criteria: The reachable capture tier is decided and the UI framework + surfaces are reported, or the scenario is explicitly tier-skipped (no UI)

levels.name: Tier-1 perf-build infra in place
levels.description: A React UI scenario carries the four perf-build infra pieces required for Tier-1 component-commit attribution: the vite profile-mode react-dom/profiling alias + esbuild keepNames, the build:profile script, the onProfilerRender util, and the top-level <React.Profiler> boundary. Non-React / tier-skipped scenarios pass this level vacuously.
exit_criteria: No perf-build-infra readiness finding is emitted (every required piece is present, or the scenario cannot reach Tier 1 by construction)

levels.name: Performance budgets honored
levels.description: The scenario's declared performance budgets (build time, bundle size, LCP, startup time-to-healthy, component-commit avg/max) are not breached by the newest persisted measurement, the native build-time floors (go/ui build thresholds from .vrooli/testing.json) hold, and no Lighthouse category scores below its configured error threshold. A breach is an ERROR that fails baseline-diff like any other health regression.
entry_criteria: Tier-1 perf-build infra is in place (or vacuous)
exit_criteria: No performance-budget breach is reported against the latest measurement/trend sample

levels.name: Trend coverage (advisory)
levels.description: ADVISORY TIER (measured, not gating). L0-L3 are the enforced gates; L4 measures whether the scenario has persisted performance trend coverage (startup benchmarks, build benchmarks, captured traces) so regressions are detectable. Gaps surface as non-blocking warnings.
exit_criteria: Advisory: persisted trend coverage exists for the applicable axes (none are blocking)

levels.name: Regression-gated, fleet-linked performance (advisory)
levels.description: ADVISORY TIER (measured, not gating). L5 measures cross-run regression gating and fleet linkage (ratcheted budgets, regression detection vs. trend, fleet offender participation). These signals are advisory: they inform fleet-readiness but never block local maturity. Only L0-L3 gate.
entry_criteria: Trend coverage is in place (L4 advisory addressed)
exit_criteria: Advisory: regression-gating and fleet-linkage findings are addressed (none are blocking)

PERF_BUDGET_BREACH_GO_BUILD.reason: A build-time-budget breach is a real performance regression that requires investigation, not a mechanical fix.

PERF_BUDGET_BREACH_UI_BUILD.reason: A UI-build-budget breach is a real performance regression that requires investigation, not a mechanical fix.

PERF_BUDGET_BREACH_BUNDLE.reason: A bundle-size-budget breach is a real performance regression that requires investigation, not a mechanical fix.

PERF_BUDGET_BREACH_LCP.reason: An LCP-budget breach is a real performance regression that requires investigation, not a mechanical fix.

PERF_BUDGET_BREACH_STARTUP.reason: A startup time-to-healthy budget breach is a real performance regression that requires investigation, not a mechanical fix.

PERF_BUDGET_BREACH_COMPONENT_COMMIT_AVG.reason: A component-commit-average budget breach is a real UI performance regression that requires investigation, not a mechanical fix.

PERF_BUDGET_BREACH_COMPONENT_COMMIT_MAX.reason: A component-commit-max budget breach is a real UI performance regression that requires investigation, not a mechanical fix.

PERF_LIGHTHOUSE_BELOW_ERROR_THRESHOLD.reason: A Lighthouse category scoring below its configured error threshold (in .vrooli/lighthouse.json) is a real UI quality/performance regression that requires investigation, not a mechanical fix. This restores the native test-genie perf phase's Lighthouse gating.

PERF_BUILD_FAILED.reason: A build that fails to compile during execution-mode benchmarking is a hard regression: the scenario cannot ship. This restores the native test-genie perf phase's early-exit-on-broken-build behavior.
